about.title: Precision orthopedic care, close to Gerugambakkam
body: Madras Ortho Clinic sits on Kundrathur Main Road in Tharapakkam, serving Gerugambakkam and the wider Mowlivakkam belt with dedicated orthopedic care — the kind that usually means a trip into central Chennai for most families in this area.

From a fracture that needs setting to a knee that's been aching for years, our approach starts with a proper clinical examination and, where needed, on-site X-rays, rather than jumping straight to a treatment plan. Surgery is recommended only when it's genuinely the right call, not the default answer.
We see the full range of orthopedic needs — sports injuries, joint pain, spine conditions, and post-fracture rehabilitation — with evening hours so a consultation doesn't mean losing a day's work.
highlights: On-site X-ray, no separate diagnostic trip
Fracture care, joint pain, and sports injury management
Evening hours until 9 PM, six days a week
Surgery recommended only when genuinely necessary

services.name: Fracture Management
services.tagline: From diagnosis to cast, handled the same visit
services.overview: For fresh fractures and breaks, we combine on-site X-ray with immediate casting or splinting, so most patients leave with a clear diagnosis and treatment plan the same day rather than being sent elsewhere for imaging first.
symptoms: Sudden pain and swelling after a fall or injury
Visible deformity or inability to bear weight
procedure: On-site digital X-ray
Fracture assessment and classification
Casting, splinting, or surgical referral as needed
Follow-up schedule for healing checks
benefits: Diagnosis and treatment in a single visit for most fractures
No separate trip to a diagnostic center for X-rays
services.recovery: Healing time varies by fracture location and severity, typically 4–8 weeks, with follow-up X-rays to confirm progress.

Stiffness that's worse in the morning or after rest
Reduced range of motion in a joint
procedure: Clinical examination and joint assessment
X-ray or further imaging if needed
Personalized pain management and mobility plan
Referral for physiotherapy or surgery only if warranted
benefits: Conservative treatment tried first wherever appropriate
Plan tailored to your specific joint and lifestyle
Clear explanation of what's actually driving the pain

faqs.answer: Not necessarily — most joint pain responds to medication, physiotherapy, and lifestyle changes. Surgery is discussed only when conservative treatment hasn't worked or the joint damage genuinely requires it.

blogPosts.title: When Joint Pain Needs More Than Rest — And When It Doesn't
blogPosts.excerpt: Not every ache needs a scan, and not every scan needs surgery. Here's how we actually decide what a joint pain case needs.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Mohan Ravindran
content: A lot of joint pain gets treated the same way by default — rest, painkillers, and a wait-and-see approach — regardless of what's actually causing it. That works for plenty of cases, but not all of them.

The first real question is whether the pain is mechanical (from overuse, alignment, or wear) or inflammatory (from a condition like arthritis). Those need genuinely different approaches, and you can usually tell the difference with a proper clinical exam and, where needed, an X-ray.

From there, most joint pain responds well to a combination of targeted exercise, activity modification, and sometimes medication — surgery is a much smaller slice of cases than people often assume, usually reserved for structural damage that conservative treatment genuinely can't fix.

The mistake we see most often isn't ignoring joint pain — it's assuming it either needs nothing or needs surgery, with nothing sensible in between. An honest assessment usually finds a middle path that gets people moving again without an operation.
